answer_1.quote: Decomposing arbitrary questions requires sophisticated natural language generation, which often relies on many, high-quality supervised examples.

answer_2.quote: To measure the fluency of decompositions, we compute the likelihood of decompositions using the pretrained GPT-2 language model. We train a BERT BASE classifier on the question-wellformedness dataset of , and we use the classifier to estimate the proportion of sub-questions that are well-formed. We measure how abstractive decompositions are by computing (i) the token Levenstein distance between the multi-hop question and its generated decomposition and (ii) the ratio between the length of the decomposition and the length of the multi-hop question.
